phasing_details.phase_detail: Single Phase (Any time within approved condition period)

description: Advertisement consent for the installation of illuminated advertising panels on either side of a BT Street Hub Unit.
decision_conditions: <span style="color: rgb(51, 51, 51);">The proposed development, by reason of its size, scale, detailed design, location, and moving digital content, fails to contribute to a safe road environment where traffic accident casualties are steadily reduced, supporting Vision Zero objectives; fails to provide a permeable pedestrian environment that is easy and safe to walk through; and fails to mitigate the negative impact on the operation of transport infrastructure, contrary to policies T1 (Strategic approach to transport), T2 (Healthy streets) and T4 (Assessing and mitigating transport impacts) of the London Plan (2021) and policies LP41 (Liveable Neighbourhoods), LP42 (Walking and Cycling), and LP43 (Transport and Development) of the Hackney Local Plan LP33 (2020).&nbsp;</span>

<p dir="ltr" style="margin: 12pt 0px; line-height: 1.38; text-align: justify; padding: 0pt 5pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space: pre-wrap;">The proposed development, by reason of its size, scale, detailed design, and method of illumination, featuring a moving digital display, would result in an obtrusive and visually incongruous feature in the historic environment that contributes to an unsightly proliferation and clutter of signage and street furniture in the street scene, and would fail to preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the conservation area, resulting in development that leads to less than substantial harm to the significance of designated heritage assets, i.e., nearby listed buildings, without substantial public benefit to outweigh the harm. As such, the proposal would be contrary to policies D3 (Optimising site capacity through the design-led approach), D4 (Delivering good design), D8 (Public realm), and HC1 (Heritage conservation and growth) of the London Plan (2021) and policies PP1 (Public Realm) and LP1 (High Quality Design), LP3, and LP7 (Advertisements) of Hackney's Local Development Plan LP33 (2020) and Hackney’s Commercial Extensions and Alterations SPD (2026).</span></p><p><br></p>

<span style="font-size:11pt"><span style="font-family:Verdana,Geneva,sans-serif">The proposed development, by reason of its size, scale, detailed design, location, and moving digital content, is likely to result in a distraction to drivers, thus failing to contribute to a safe road environment where traffic accident casualties are steadily reduced, supporting Vision Zero objectives. It fails to provide a permeable pedestrian environment that is easy and safe to walk through, and fails to mitigate the negative impact on the operation of transport infrastructure, contrary to policies T1 (Strategic approach to transport), T2 (Healthy streets) and T4 (Assessing and mitigating transport impacts) of the London Plan (2021) and policies LP41 (Liveable Neighbourhoods), LP42 (Walking and Cycling), and LP43 (Transport and Development) of the Hackney Local Plan LP33 (2020).&nbsp;</span></span>
